facts.text: The study arc-melted an equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy, remelted it at least five times, and compared its mechanical behavior with commercially sourced powder-sintered pure tungsten.
Room-temperature uniaxial compression was performed on 4 mm × 4 mm cylindrical specimens at an engineering strain rate of 0.001 s^-1.
Indentation plastometry used 5 mm cubes, a 1 mm-radius Si3N4 indenter, loads up to 5 kN, and temperatures from room temperature to 500 °C in 100 °C increments.
Room-temperature scratch tests used a 200 µm-radius Rockwell C diamond stylus at a constant 100 N normal load and 0.01 mm/s over a 3 mm track.
Solidification produced two BCC phases arranged as W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions, with V distributed between both regions.
The alloy's high strength was attributed to multicomponent solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and frictional resistance associated especially with W and Ta.

The improved plasticity and damage tolerance were interpreted as effects of Ti, V, and Zr through dislocation-core modification, improved grain-boundary cohesion, localized plasticity, and impeded crack propagation rather than being established by isolated causal tests.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr retained higher indentation-derived yield strength from room temperature through 500 °C.
The alloy's indentation-derived yield strength decreased from about 1.66 GPa at room temperature to about 650 MPa at 500 °C, where it remained more than 2.5 times tungsten's approximately 250 MPa.
Bulk room-temperature compression of WTaTiVZr produced about 1.6 GPa yield strength, 1.8 GPa ultimate compressive strength, and 6% plastic strain before shear-dominated quasi-cleavage fracture.
Indentation cracks disappeared above 200 °C in WTaTiVZr, whereas tungsten did not show comparable ductile behavior until around 400 °C.
WTaTiVZr formed shallower, more uniform scratch grooves with fewer cracks and had a fracture toughness of about 38 ± 1 MPa√m versus 25 ± 1 MPa√m for tungsten, an increase of approximately 52%.
